acceptanceResults.environment: Actual rc.3 Host with frozen DS and offline fixture model on isolated Win11 Node24; real restart and zero real model calls
acceptanceResults.notes: Separate real Host flows verify UI HTTP resend, duplicate message_bot and cold-start replay. Each returns the original receipt or current Task without another worker delivery. After an explicit retry, cold replay preserves the current Task/operation and two attempts with zero backend dispatch. Existing canonical plan replay remains covered.

Current native tests reject cycles, self/dangling/duplicate dependencies, duplicate package ids, unknown target Bots, executable paths, MCP URLs, secrets, invalid effects and unknown fields before scheduling. The actual default Host uses the same validator before rows or provider dispatch and rejects a Worker plan targeting Main outside its delegation scope. This covers every T08 criterion without real model inference; deployment and other scenarios remain separate.
acceptanceResults.environment: Win11 / Node24.20.0 / SQLite13.0.3; actual rc.3 default Host with offline fixture model and native plan validator

acceptanceResults.notes: Current journal/service scenarios prove direct and transitive downstream blocking while independent read and cross-Bot branches succeed and the parent finishes failed rather than succeeded. The actual default Host exercises the same dependency plan and preserves legacy serial managed Task behavior. Real remote-write confirms failure blocks only the downstream package, and cold restart retains dependency edges and identities. All T09 criteria are covered; other scenarios and deployment acceptance remain separate.
acceptanceResults.environment: Win11 / Node24.20.0 / SQLite13.0.3; actual rc.3 default Host with offline fixture model and native SQLite journal
Win11 / Node24.20.0 / SQLite13.0.3; actual default Host plus native service with 24 packages across two Bots
acceptanceResults.notes: The default Host runs two managed Tasks concurrently with maxConcurrentTasks 2. The new real service load test submits 24 packages across two Bots with per-Bot concurrency 2 and service-wide active cap 4: every per-Bot maximum is <=2, total/machine activity is <=4, ready/running waiting is visible, all 24 settle succeeded with one original attempt and exactly 24 backend calls. No loss, duplicate dispatch or busy-loop dispatch is observed; unrelated deadline expiry and cancellation evidence remains.

Real Agent writes on the same physical root or alias are rejected while independent roots and reads proceed. Workspace admission is visible across connections, a real terminal fs_write receipt releases the root for a successor, and unknown outcomes retain it until original-operation reconciliation. Current revalidation passes 40 of 44 with four Linux-only root-lock cases skipped on Windows; earlier three-platform evidence covers those paths. This satisfies the T11 worktree mutex criteria without claiming full OS or deployment acceptance.
acceptanceResults.environment: Win11 / Node24.20.0 / SQLite13.0.3; real Agent physical roots and native journal
Real Ubuntu Node22 Docker 29.1.3 and offline native CLI child/grandchild; isolated fixtures; Win11 regression with explicit Linux-only skips
acceptanceResults.notes: One real plan concurrently runs CLI and remote command branches. Whole-tree cancellation preserves one original attempt per active package, skips the join and creates no second CLI process. Native-tree proof plus /proc verifies both CLI PIDs stopped; container-supervisor proof and one original Agent operation verify the remote stop. Unconfirmed stop remains cancelling and cannot retry. Ubuntu related tests pass 34/34; Windows has 28 pass, zero failures and six Linux-only skips.

acceptanceResults.environment: Win11 / Node24.20.0 / SQLite13.0.3; real process-exit native suites and actual rc.3 default Host cold start
acceptanceResults.notes: Real process exits cover pre-dispatch, post-dispatch and receipt-persistence boundaries. Recovery restores the original attempt/operation, keeps unknown work unreplayed, restores committed receipts without another model call or invoice and preserves original artifacts. The actual default Host reconstructs Bot identity, grants, machines and bindings. Current revalidation has 67 passing checks; the journal suite was run through integration-task-probe with the verified SQLite driver as required. T13 criteria are covered without claiming production power-loss or every external provider exactly-once.

acceptanceResults.environment: Win11 / Node24.20.0 / SQLite13.0.3; real independent Agent process killed after a successful write and restarted on a new loopback port
acceptanceResults.notes: The real Agent commits the file and succeeded receipt before its process is killed. The Host then loses the reply and becomes needs-reconciliation with outcome unknown. After a normal Agent restart and endpoint re-pair, the Host reconciles the original operation to succeeded with exactly one fs_write call and one operation row; the file is unchanged. This covers the real network break/restore criterion without replaying the action. Other command and deployment scenarios remain separate.

acceptanceResults.environment: Win11 / Node24.20.0 / SQLite13.0.3; real Agent remote-write plus native journal
acceptanceResults.notes: The same request returns the original Task/operation and a changed digest conflicts. A dedicated real product flow now deletes the produced file after success and resubmits: the original succeeded identity is returned with one fs_write and one operation row, and the file is not recreated. Dedup also survives fresh connections and archived runs. All T15 criteria are covered without implying that dedup rolls back or restores artifacts.

Invalid or revoked credentials fail uniformly before tool admission with no operation row. Public read models, diagnostics and SQLite never contain pairing tokens, and host-only secret UI prevents Bot sharing. E113 closes a real leak: resolveSecret exceptions containing an endpoint/token are now normalized to MACHINE_SECRET_UNAVAILABLE instead of propagating private text into model-facing errors. New regression asserts no tool action and no secret in error text, projection or database. Existing 401 and audit redaction evidence covers the remaining criteria.

acceptanceResults.notes: Revoked grants, stale approvals and outdated machine/workspace revisions cannot admit new actions. Workspace roots-generation changes fence unsettled writes without blocking reads or impersonating a subject. Current revalidation passes 49/49 across capability authority, remote machines/auth, remote write and workspace generation. T17 criteria are covered without claiming every external launcher or deployment boundary.
